diagrams.title: Powered Land Qualification, From Megawatts Back to Dirt
diagrams.subtitle: Start from available power, then work backward to acreage, line, redundancy and site control
diagrams.caption: Power is the site and acreage follows. Powered land trades at about 4x to 5x unpowered land in current data center deals (datacenterHawk).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order follows the practitioner operator gates. Acreage, study-cost, run-out and upfront-security figures are attributed practitioner claims from Franklin Andrew Cruz, Advanta IRA (Mike Embry), datacenterHawk and Systems Leverage, not independent estimates.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Franklin Andrew Cruz (YrpzmGX0-YM), Advanta IRA (3rM3iGzRRUA), datacenterHawk (dTHn2ejpXvM) and Systems Leverage (nx4eX4emlwE).

stages.label: Call the utility for 100MW-plus
stages.detail: Ask directly whether the utility can support 100MW or more; the call routes to the department handling 50MW-plus loads, the desk that matters (Franklin Andrew Cruz).

stages.label: Screen acreage at 1MW per acre
stages.detail: Hold a 100-acre floor; below it, AI data center buyers will not look at the site (Franklin Andrew Cruz).

stages.label: Pin the plan to a named line
stages.detail: Tie the concept plan to a specific line such as a 230 and keep a multifamily or Kroger commercial Plan B ready before paying the study fee; Embry cites $60k to $140k spent to get the power company answer, and power run-outs at $20M per mile (Advanta IRA).

stages.label: Name the redundancy source
stages.detail: Identify a gas or coal plant for redundancy before advancing; Embry's Decatur, Alabama site in TVA territory died for lack of one (Advanta IRA).

stages.label: Lock the dirt with an option contract
stages.detail: Control land through options, from 2-3 year solar options to Stargate's $1 option; one deal required $22M posted upfront to secure power after zoning (Advanta IRA, Systems Leverage).

diagrams.title: Hosting Capacity Funnel, From Campus Load to Feeder Headroom
diagrams.subtitle: Published hosting values are screening ceilings, not connection rights
diagrams.caption: A 60 MW facility load against a live distribution feeder demo shows how fast mapped headroom narrows; one month of delay on a 60 MW facility can cost up to $14 million (KorrAI).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Values are the cited MW figures at each screen. Stages 2, 3 and 5 come from Dan Rogers' Foxboro 2 feeder demo; stage 4 is a separate National Grid portal ceiling example. Conversion text describes the screen applied, not a computed rate.
diagrams.note: Attributed to KorrAI (MvUw50RZNRQ) and National Grid Distributed Generation, Dan Rogers (KxAPuQUu_II).

stages.label: 60 MW data center target load
stages.conversion: Reference load KorrAI prices at up to $14M per month of delay
stages.detail: Screen geology, karst, sinkholes and water tables before earthworks (KorrAI).

stages.label: Foxboro 2 substation bank rating
stages.conversion: Distribution bank sits far below a campus-scale load
stages.detail: Live Massachusetts portal demo (National Grid Distributed Generation).

stages.label: Feeder available hosting capacity
stages.conversion: Published value is a screening ceiling, not a connection right
stages.detail: No ASO pending and high side protection already present, so 3V0 was not needed.

stages.label: Mapped value treated as a ceiling
stages.conversion: A recloser without voltage supervisory control drags downstream values lower
stages.detail: Separate National Grid portal example of a mapped upper limit.

stages.label: DG already connected on the feeder
stages.conversion: Switch to connected plus pending to see the real queue
stages.detail: Aggregate pending DG usually triggers an ASO study (National Grid Distributed Generation).

diagrams.title: ERCOT Large-Load Queue, Paper Megawatts to Forecast
diagrams.subtitle: Headline load requests haircut to what forecasters actually count
diagrams.caption: The large-load queue is mostly paper; Dominion's zone shows 70 GW of requests against a 24 GW peak, and ERCOT Batch Zero demands $50,000/MW security to separate capitalized projects.
diagrams.assumptions_note: 438 GW, 218 GW and 148 GW are attributed practitioner figures. The 220 GW and 290 GW bars are simple arithmetic differences between those figures, not separately reported counts. The 218 GW and 148 GW figures are as of July 2025.
diagrams.note: Adjusted forecast attributed to Data Centers Technical Info (S8vmSHwFrvE); Batch Zero security attributed to WhyPKD (EvpNriZrrME); workshop mechanics from James Dickey (9zpO8wwsfXc).

bars.label: Outside TSP letters, contracts or forecasts

diagrams.title: Hyperscale Lead Times, Buildings Versus Power
diagrams.subtitle: Buildings rise faster than the grid, transformers and turbines can arrive
diagrams.caption: Power, not chips or buildings, is the scarce input; order long-lead electrical gear immediately because you cannot download another transformer.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Min and max are the cited ranges. Typical is the midpoint of each cited range, shown only for bar placement. Grid gear is cited as two-plus years and plotted at 2. Turbine waits span the practitioner disagreement from 2-3 years to more than 5.
diagrams.note: Transformer and grid gear lead times attributed to BUILT BENEATH (7L7MfK9coTY); early ordering guidance from MEP Engineer AJ (lTK_pU1_uFc); bottleneck framing from The Power Engineer (BWtk0CSPH6g).

diagrams.title: Cost-of-Waiting Gate Before Committing to a Queue Position
diagrams.subtitle: The plug, not the panel or the chip, sets the clock
diagrams.caption: Median 2025 builds waited 61 months from request to commercial operation, versus 36 months in 2015 and 22 months in 2008 (THE PHYSICAL LAYER).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is a screening sequence assembled from practitioner operator gates. Per-kW benchmarks, attrition shares and the $598M upgrade bill are attributed practitioner claims drawn from Berkeley Lab and PJM study figures they cited.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Wattlore (CDd-hsI3tKQ), The Pharos Project (Br7K7fGD4uk), US Energy Weekly (DzkVggOvJGs) and learnBESS (m0yVO4ZOmdc).

nodes.question: Divided by project kW, is the network upgrade estimate near the roughly $84/kW completed projects paid rather than the roughly $600/kW of projects that quit?
nodes.fail_action: Re-price or exit; one 51 MW New Jersey solar farm drew a $598M bill, more than $11,000 per kW (Wattlore).

nodes.question: Are the projects ahead of you solid, with attrition priced in and the queue number quoted with its date?
nodes.fail_action: Haircut the headline queue; only about 13% of 2000-2020 requested capacity came online and 75% withdrew (The Pharos Project).

nodes.question: On an ERCOT connect-and-manage site, is curtailment modeled for when the wires are full?
nodes.fail_action: Model curtailment before committing, because it hits revenue directly (US Energy Weekly).

nodes.question: Can arbitrage, balancing and capacity be stacked through one route-to-market provider?
nodes.fail_action: Rework the revenue case; a single stream rarely justifies the investment (learnBESS).

diagrams.title: BESS at the Data Center Integration Team
diagrams.subtitle: Grid-forming storage as the price of interconnection, not an add-on
diagrams.caption: AI training loads jump 30-60% in milliseconds and mass-trip on voltage dips; Lyten reports flattening up to 99.5% of load-step volatility in controlled tests (Volta Foundation).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Spoke roles map practitioner specialties to integration functions; no speaker prescribed this org chart or a headcount. KPI figures are attributed claims from the named firms.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Keentel Engineering (BTkszCEW7nY), Digital Infrastructure Network for ABB (U2apRbTTZuE), UL Solutions (TtbHyJ6xzNg), ALL4 Environmental Consultants (-B0ACVnCSu0) and Rand Simulation (LBt7MoTnFFQ).

center.focus: Grid-forming BESS sized to buffer AI load swings and carry islanding behind the gensets

spokes.kpi: Validated vendor models, EMT and harmonic studies, and TDD at the PCC confirmed before the purchase order

spokes.type: Equipment OEM (ABB via Digital Infrastructure Network)
spokes.kpi: 20 ms full-load pickup; islanding under 0.5 s including upstream breaker opening

spokes.type: Listing body and permitting advisers (UL Solutions, ALL4)
spokes.kpi: UL 9540 listing plus full-scale fire test; 100 kWh at 2 ft triggers the NFPA 855 Chapter 9 test
Full-site airflow run at 30% and 60% design under moderate wind; intake held below 54C

diagrams.title: Interconnection Cost per kW Across Cluster Studies
diagrams.subtitle: Cost follows impact, not MW, and your costs are coupled to your neighbors
diagrams.total_range: $0 to $2,700/kW across cited interconnection cost studies
diagrams.caption: Price the withdrawal ladder before posting; on 200 MW with $178M allocated, exits run $8.9M at 5%, $17.88M at 10% and $35.6M at 20% (Keentel Engineering).
diagrams.assumptions_note: Buckets compare cited per-kW figures from different regions and datasets; they are not additive. Single-value buckets carry equal low and high values.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Environmental Defense Fund, Sarah Johnson (M62wgLYBKBw), and Keentel Engineering (TM7qt8CCWxk).

buckets.label: PJM cost, median to 90th percentile
buckets.notes: Hand-collected PJM dataset of about 4,000 requests and 7,000 studies (Environmental Defense Fund).

buckets.label: Kill-risk flag line
buckets.notes: Above $100/kW makes withdrawal 22 percentage points more likely; 13% of estimates move more than $100/kW between studies.

buckets.label: ISO-NE transitional cluster allocation
buckets.notes: 23 projects, 4,826.5 MW, $3.21B total upgrade cost; $0 to $541M per project (Keentel Engineering).

buckets.label: Install cost reference
buckets.notes: Roughly $1,500/kW to install, the benchmark against which the PJM cost tail is read.

diagrams.title: Community Due-Diligence Sprint for Hyperscale Siting
diagrams.subtitle: Opposition is organized and winning votes, so diligence starts before the hearing
diagrams.caption: 65% of residents oppose local sites, Palm Beach County denied Project Tango's expansion 5-1, and 40 of 41 Ohio county ballot initiatives ban sites above 25 MW.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week buckets are a sequencing frame for practitioner operator gates; no speaker prescribed a four-week schedule. Permit checks continue monthly after Week 2.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Democracy Now! (Ac0-fBK0LVQ), Careers Over Beers Podcast (S_6FoEr75bs), PBS NewsHour (fkB8mt1DEVw) and Jeff Pierson (CmmE71lfGdw).

weeks.title: Read the lease offer
weeks.deliverable: Flag any NDA or 'temporary' lease offer as the opening move of a data-center deal
weeks.gate: Organizers report solar pitches pivoting to hyperscale after signature (Democracy Now!)

weeks.title: Pull generator air permits
weeks.deliverable: Check diesel-generator air-permit filings, then repeat once a month
weeks.gate: Backup generation caught before it surfaces at a hearing (Careers Over Beers Podcast)

weeks.title: Test noise and water claims
weeks.deliverable: Demand dBC or dBZ fence-line readings for 24/7 operation and ask whether a closed loop is filled once or draws water every day
weeks.gate: No reliance on dBA-only numbers (Careers Over Beers Podcast, PBS NewsHour)

weeks.title: Document the siting posture
weeks.deliverable: Record every factor behind the siting position
weeks.gate: Documentation, not the score itself, is the legal shield (Jeff Pierson)
